etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English, from Old French, from Latin mōbilis (“easy to be moved, moveable”), from moveō (“move”).

definitions.definition: Capable of being moved, especially on wheels.
Pertaining to or by agency of mobile phones.

quote.citation: 2012 December 1, “An internet of airborne things”, in The Economist‎[1], volume 405, number 8813, page 3 (Technology Quarterly):
quote.text: A farmer could place an order for a new tractor part by text message and pay for it by mobile money-transfer. A supplier many miles away would then take the part to the local matternet station for airborne dispatch via drone.

definitions.definition: Characterized by an extreme degree of fluidity; moving or flowing with great freedom.
Easily moved in feeling, purpose, or direction; excitable; changeable; fickle.

quote.citation: 1850, Nathaniel Hawthorne, chapter 7, in The Scarlet Letter, a Romance, Boston, Mass.: Ticknor, Reed, and Fields, →OCLC:
quote.text: the quick and mobile curiosity of her disposition

definitions.definition: Changing in appearance and expression under the influence of the mind.

quote.citation: 1837, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], “Another London Life”, in Ethel Churchill: Or, The Two Brides. […], volume I, London: Henry Colburn, […], →OCLC, page 176:
quote.text: His finely cut features were capable of every variety of expression; they were, to use a French epithet, expressive as their epithets for all social qualities usually are, mobile in the extreme.

definitions.definition: (biology) Capable of being moved, aroused, or excited; capable of spontaneous movement.
(sculpture) A kinetic sculpture or decorative arrangement made of items hanging so that they can move independently from each other.
(telephony, UK, Ireland) Ellipsis of mobile phone.

quote.citation: 2000, “Idioteque”, in Kid A, performed by Radiohead:
quote.text: Mobiles squerking, mobiles chirping / Take the money and run

definitions.definition: (uncountable, Internet) The internet accessed via mobile devices.
One who moves or can move (e.g. to travel).
